about: Which SCATS detectors count cars at the stop line, per approach, at the junctions around the Swanston closure (CBD), and around the test TGS on Swanston St between Faraday St and Grattan St (sites 4391 to 4425). Read by hand from DTP Traffic Signal Configuration Data Sheets (CC-BY 4.0), 30 Sep 2026. Bike, tram, queue, hook-turn box and pedestrian detectors are left out. 'no_car_approaches' are approaches where the network has a car edge but the sheet shows no general car traffic, so the simulation gets a count of zero there. 'all_car_approaches_counted' marks sites whose car total is complete, used to correct sites without a sheet. Approaches not listed are left unconstrained. A detector written as 'site:detector' belongs to another site's controller.

2921.name: SWANSTON/LATROBE
2921.notes: Detector 3 (Swanston St southbound, on the closed block) extends the southbound bike signal SG8 and the right turn SG5, so it counts mostly bikes (about 1,800 a day) and is not used. OpenStreetMap has no southbound car lane there. No detector counts the northbound car lane into the closed block. Detectors 18 and 19 are a second set at the La Trobe St tram stop crossing and duplicate La Trobe St traffic.

2920.name: RUSSELL/LATROBE
2920.notes: Detectors 13 and 14 are hook-turn boxes inside the junction (about 6,900 a day each) and detector 12 a queue loop; all left out.

2922.name: ELIZABETH/LATROBE
2922.notes: Map is rotated; orientation from grades and sign notes. Detectors 11, 12 and 19 are hook-turn boxes (about 5,000 a day each for 11 and 19) and are left out. Kerb lanes are shared with bikes.

2904.name: SWANSTON/LONSDALE
2904.notes: Swanston St here is trams, bikes and permitted vehicles only (detectors 1 to 4 are kerb lanes with bike-like counts or sit in the tram tracks), and netconvert opens it to cars, so both Swanston approaches get zero. Lonsdale St kerb lanes are bus lanes (detectors 5 and 8, under 900 a day each) and are left out. Detectors 15 and 16 are Caledonian Lane.

2906.name: ELIZABETH/LONSDALE
2906.notes: Elizabeth St has no car detectors (permanent green extension), so its approaches are unconstrained.

2914.name: ELIZABETH/LITTLE LONSDALE
2914.notes: Southbound detector 9 has no August 2026 data, so the southbound approach is unconstrained.

4512.name: ELIZABETH/A'BECKETT
4512.notes: Elizabeth St has no detectors. Detectors 3 and 4 are call-only loops inside the junction that duplicate 1 and 2.

4523.name: SWANSTON/FRANKLIN
4523.notes: The sheet predates the current layout: detectors 2, 4 and 6 are off or unused on it but count traffic in 2026. Westbound 4 looks like car traffic and is used. Southbound 3 is the right turn only; the southbound left turn (detector 2, 732 a day) is left out, so southbound is a lower bound. Detector 6 (3,900 a day) can't be placed.

2913.name: SWANSTON/LITTLE LONSDALE
2913.notes: Swanston St here is the permit-only section, which netconvert opens to cars. Detector 1 (northbound right turn in the tram lane, about 1,800 a day) is left out and the northbound edge gets zero, to keep general cars off it.

4392.name: SWANSTON/FARADAY/MONASH
4392.notes: The site also runs the pedestrian crossing at the Melbourne University tram stop, inside the block south of Faraday St: detector 1 counts northbound cars there (the same cars as detector 2 at the Faraday St stop line) and detector 5 counts southbound cars there, about 2,300 a weekday. Detector 5 is the count of the lane the test TGS closes; it is used as the southbound approach of 4391. Detectors 6 and 9 are bike loops, 10 to 23 tram inputs, 24 to 28 push buttons. Eastbound is Monash Rd, the university entry.

4391.name: GRATTAN/SWANSTON
4391.notes: The sheet is from 2014, before the junction was rebuilt. Grattan St detectors 5 to 10 still count plausible car volumes (they agree with 4395 and 4425 on either side). The sheet's Swanston St detectors do not: 2 and 4 (right-turn lanes that no longer exist) read zero, 1 and 3 report only 8 days in the month, and 11 and 12, 'not used' on the sheet, now count about 4,300 a day each. So the southbound approach uses detector 5 of site 4392, which counts the same lane 150 m upstream with no side street between, and the northbound approach is left unconstrained. Detectors 13 to 16 are tram loops, 17 to 20 push buttons.

4395.name: GRATTAN/CARDIGAN
4395.notes: One loop across all lanes of each approach. Detectors 5 and 6 are push buttons.

4393.name: SWANSTON/ELGIN
4393.notes: Detectors 1, 3 and 8 are bike detectors (8 reports about 10,000 a day, so it is not a usable count). 10 and 14 are tram loops, 16 a tram push button. Eastbound is Tin Alley.

4425.name: GRATTAN/BOUVERIE
4425.notes: Detectors 1 and 3 are bike loops, 7 and 8 bus detectors in the eastbound bus lane, 9 and 10 push buttons.

4396.name: GRATTAN/LYGON
4396.notes: Old sheet, but the eight lane detectors add up to the site total. Detectors 9 to 12 are push buttons. Detector 3 reports only 12 days in the month.

4407.name: LYGON/FARADAY
4407.notes: Old sheet, but the eight lane detectors add up to the site total. Detectors 9 to 12 are push buttons.
